text: {"question":"How does the Brownian‑motion–driven coupling between dark matter and dark radiation, which causes dark matter to absorb many light kicks, affect the background evolution equations that involve the interaction rate Q with dark energy?","reference_answer":"The frequent, small‑momentum exchanges between dark matter and dark radiation act like a viscous drag, effectively transferring energy from the dark matter fluid to the radiation bath. In the background equations this manifests as an additional source term proportional to the interaction rate Q, which itself is taken to be proportional to the dark‑energy density. Thus the coupling modifies the dark‑matter continuity equation by adding a term ξHρ_ide, while the dark‑energy equation gains a corresponding sink term, ensuring total energy conservation while reflecting the momentum diffusion caused by the Brownian motion of dark matter in the dark‑radiation fluid."}
